# lean-pkg report

read-only: a redacted bug report in the repository's issue format; dry run unless --yes (files it with gh issue create).

## Usage

```text
lean-pkg report [--command ARGS] [--body TEXT] [--from-log FILE[:N]] [--package NAME]
                [--title TITLE] [--enhancement] [--target-repo OWNER/NAME] [--dry-run]
                [--yes] [--json]
```

## Arguments and flags

| Argument or flag | Description |
|---|---|
| `--command ARGS` | the lean-pkg arguments to capture, quoted as one string ("status NAME"); re-run in a subprocess (with --json when the subcommand has it) unless it would write; a value starting with '-' needs --command=VALUE |
| `--body TEXT` | free text for What happened, nothing re-run (before the re-run when --command is given too); redacted like everything else |
| `--from-log FILE[:N]` | the last N lines (default 200) of a stage log, under Log excerpt in What happened; redacted like everything else; a missing file is a usage error |
| `--package NAME` | add the package's registry record (status, lease, receipt commits); its .lean-pkg-private-patterns joins the redaction |
| `--title TITLE` | issue title (default: report: &lt;the command&gt;, else report: lean-pkg &lt;version&gt;) |
| `--enhancement` | label enhancement instead of bug |
| `--target-repo OWNER/NAME` | repository to file on (default lean-pkg/lean-pkg) (old spelling --repo, kept working) |
| `--dry-run` | print title, labels and body; file nothing (default) |
| `--yes` | file it with `gh issue create` and print the URL (needs `gh auth login`) |

## Details

| Form | What it does | Key flags |
|---|---|---|
| `report` | read-only: assemble a bug report in the shape of `.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/bug_report.md` (same section headings, same order) and, with `--yes`, file it on `lean-pkg/lean-pkg` with `gh issue create --label bug` (`--label enhancement` with `--enhancement`; `--repo OWNER/NAME` for a fork) and print the issue URL. Filled automatically: **Version** (the `--version` line, Python version, platform; the `ok`/`warn` lines of `doctor --json`; the `comparator host-check --json` verdict); **Command** and **What happened** with `--command "ARGS"` (the lean-pkg arguments as one string; a value starting with `-` needs `--command=ARGS`): the command re-run in a subprocess, with `--json` appended when it is not there and the subcommand has the flag, its exit code, stdout and stderr (a long stream keeps its first 150 and last 50 lines); a command that would write (the registry or event log, `wiki --out`, `formalization --write/--out`, `comparator config`, `index render/migrate`, `claims migrate`) is not re-run and the body says so; `--body TEXT` (free text, nothing re-run) and `--from-log FILE[:N]` (the last N lines, default 200, of a stage log, under a `Log excerpt` line with the redacted path) go first in **What happened**, before the re-run when `--command` is given too; at least one of `--command`, `--body`, `--from-log` is required; **Minimal registry or receipt** with `--package NAME`: the record's status, visibility, `lean_toolchain`, lease fields with `expires_at`, and the gate and comparator receipt paths with the commits they bind; **Checklist** ticked from what is known (`--json` used, `validate` passes). Redaction is mandatory and applies to every captured text, the title, body text and log excerpt included, in this order: in the sections report attaches itself (version, doctor, host-check, the record, the re-run's stdout and stderr) only, every record's and lease's `agent`, `workspace` and `contact` value to `<agent>`, `<workspace>`, `<contact>`; the registry file to `<registry>`, its directory to `<registry-dir>`, every record's checkout (stored, `$HOME`-joined and resolved) to `<checkout>`, the user-level default registry, when another one, to `<user-default-registry>`/`<user-default-registry-dir>`, the other local paths doctor and the version line name, whole (stored and resolved): lean-pkg's package directory to `<lean-pkg-install>`, an editable install's checkout to `<lean-pkg-checkout>`, the Python executable to `<python>`, the git work tree holding the registry to `<registry-repo>`, the index directory to `<index-dir>`, an event log that is not the registry's sibling to `<events-path>`; the home directory to `~`; then the `public-safety` scanner (its built-in families, the `--package` checkout's and the registry directory's `.lean-pkg-private-patterns`, the names derived from every record's `local_path`, `agent`, `workspace` and lease; email addresses always), each match `[…]`. Each redacted section is scanned again, line by line: the user's own text (title, `--command`, `--body`, `--from-log`, `--package`) and every attached section, not the report's own fixed prose (a derived name can be an ordinary word such as `home`). A private name in the user's own text is redacted (`[…]`), not refused; the guard refuses only what redaction left. A blocking hit left refuses, exit 1, nothing filed, the hit families listed (`--json` `families[]`) and the sections named, in text ("in your text (--body)", "in an attached section (doctor)") and in `--json` `sections[]` {`section`, `origin` `user` or `attached`, `families`}. Default is a dry run: print the title, labels, repository, redaction count and body, exit 0. `--yes` refuses, exit 1 with the `gh auth login` hint, when `gh` is not on PATH or `gh auth status` fails. `--json`: `ok`, `filed`, `url` (null unless filed), `title`, `labels[]`, `body`, `redactions` (replacements made), and `log_excerpt` {path (redacted), lines (included)} with `--from-log`. Usage errors (none of `--command`/`--body`/`--from-log`, an empty or unsplittable `--command`, an empty `--body`, a missing `--from-log` file or an `N` that is not a positive integer, `--repo` not `OWNER/NAME`, an empty `--title`, `--dry-run` with `--yes`) exit 2 | `[--command ARGS]` `[--body TEXT]` `[--from-log FILE[:N]]` `[--package NAME]` `[--title T]` `[--enhancement]` `[--repo OWNER/NAME]` `[--dry-run\|--yes]` |

## Exit codes

0 success (dry runs and no-ops included), 1 refused or failed, 2 usage error; see [Exit codes](../cli.md#exit-codes).

Exit 1 is also a negative answer here:

- `report --yes`: a blocking public-safety hit left, or gh missing or logged out

## Examples

Assemble a redacted bug report (version, doctor and host-check lines, the command re-run with its output, the package's record) and print it; a dry run by default that files nothing.

```bash
lean-pkg report --command "status my-proof" --package my-proof
```

Sample output:

```text
title: report: lean-pkg status my-proof
labels: bug
repository: lean-pkg/lean-pkg
redactions: 15
---
...
```

File it on lean-pkg/lean-pkg with `gh issue create` and print the issue URL; refused with exit 1 when gh is missing or not logged in (a blocking private-pattern hit left after redaction refuses in either mode).

```bash
lean-pkg report --from-log logs/build.log:100 --body "lake build hangs at Mathlib.Order" --yes
```
